messages.subject: Reactivity vs. Static data
parts:
I'm not sure if this is entirely possible, but I am attempting to build a dynamic distribution display tool. I have everything working as of right now but have hit a bit of a wall.

In the current version, the user selects a certain data distribution, a number of observations to take, the number of sample means to take, and the sample size for the each sample mean. I then have two plots output, the first just showing the sample distribution, and the second showing the distribution of the sample mean at that point. However, the sample mean distribution is "too reactive". By that I mean, every time the number of sample means changes, it starts the sampling process over. Instead, I would like it to take 1 sample of say "n" observations and then stay put. At this point, as the number of sample means changes, each sample comes from the dataset (not generate a new data set to sample from for each concurrent sample mean calculation. That result should be stored into a vector or data frame, and the second plot will build upon itself as the number of sample means increases.

I have not deployed this yet so I will post the raw code below to hopefully give a better idea of what I'm doing.

ui.R

library(shiny)

# UI definition for distribution tool
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  
  # title
  headerPanel("Distribution Visualization Tool"),
  
  # Sidebar for choosing distribution type, sample size, # of means, etc.
  sidebarPanel(
    radioButtons("dist", "Distribution type:",
                 list("Normal" = "norm",
                      "Uniform" = "unif",
                      "Log-normal" = "lnorm",
                      "Exponential" = "exp")),
    br(),
    

    sliderInput("n", 
                "Number of observations:", 
                value = 500,
                min = 1, 
                max = 5000),
    
    # animation looping for number of sample means to take
    # note: interval controls the speed in ms between steps
    
    sliderInput("N",
                "Number of Sample Means:", 1,100,1,step=1,
                animate=animationOptions(interval=500, loop=T)),
    
    sliderInput("xbar.size",
                "Sample Size for Sample Mean:",
                value = 5,
                min = 1,
                max = 500)
  ),
  
  # Present information in 2 tabs: plot and data summary
  mainPanel(
    tabsetPanel(
      tabPanel("Plot", plotOutput("plot1"),plotOutput("plot2")), 
      tabPanel("Summary", verbatimTextOutput("summary1"),verbatimTextOutput("summary2")) 
    )
  )
))

server.R

library(shiny)

# server logic
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  
  #generate data from selected distribution
  data <- reactive({  
    dist <- switch(input$dist,
                   norm = rnorm,
                   unif = runif,
                   lnorm = rlnorm,
                   exp = rexp,
                   rnorm)
    
    dist(input$n)
  })
  

####
this is the chunk of the code that I think will need to change
####

  means <- reactive({
    if(input$xbar.size<input$n){    
    sample.means<-numeric(input$N)
    for(i in 1:input$N)
    sample.means[i]<-mean(sample(data(),input$xbar.size,FALSE))
    sample.means
   }
  })
  
  # Plot the underlying distribution on top, and the distribution
  # of the sample mean on bottom.
  output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
    dist <- input$dist
    n <- input$n
    
    hist(data(), 
         main=paste("Observations: ",'r', dist, " ~ (",round(mean(data()),3),",",round(sd(data()),3),")", sep=''))
  })
  
  output$plot2 <- renderPlot({
    dist <- input$dist
    n <- input$n
    
    hist(means(),xlim=c(mean(data())-2*sd(data()),mean(data())+2*sd(data())),
         main=paste("Sample Means: Approximately ~ N(",round(mean(means()),3),",",round(sd(means()),3),")",sep=''))
  })
  
  # Generate a summary of the data
  output$summary1 <- renderPrint({
    summary(data())
  })
  
  output$summary2 <- renderPrint({
    summary(means())
  })
  
})


I'm not sure if there is a way to have selective reactivity for a reactive function, or a way to store static values from a reactive function as it changes for future accessing or what, but would appreciate any help anyone can offer.

Thanks in advance!

Jb

messages.subject: Re: Reactivity vs. Static data
parts:
Oh, it was not clear that you wanted to keep previous values.

Here is one way you can do it:

#define a data set outside your server function, say allData.
allMeans <- NULL

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

#in your data function update this one:

means <- reactive({
    if(input$xbar.size<input$n){    
    sample.means<-numeric(input$N)
    for(i in 1:input$N)
    sample.means[i]<-mean(sample(data(),input$xbar.size,FALSE))

allMeans <<- c(allMeans,sample.means)
    allMeans
   }
  })

This should do what you want. The problem is for a given user, this value will persist as long as the session does - even if the refresh. What you need to add is a button that will set allMeans to NULL when it is clicked.

There might be a simpler way to do this but this should work.
